manifest.description: Suggest cohesive method/field clusters inside a Java god-class for partition-decision review. Analysis-only — walks the method-to-field and method-to-method affinity graph and proposes extract_java_class-shaped clusters with name hints, move_fields, cross-cluster calls, and expected delegate/callback wiring. Operator picks which (if any) to round-trip into extract_java_class.
when_to_use: auditing a god-class and wanting partition suggestions before committing to extract_java_class
the dependency graph already exists (java-class-dependency-graph) and the operator wants the next step — proposed splits, not raw inventory
scoring competing partition shapes by internal cohesion vs cross-cluster coupling
anti_patterns: do not use as a refactor — this atom emits proposals, not edits
do not auto-apply a suggested cluster — operator must review move_fields, expected_wiring, and cross_cluster_calls before issuing extract_java_class
do not use on a class with a single method or no instance fields — clustering signal is undefined

source.description: File containing the target class, relative to project_dir.

module_name.description: Class name to cluster. Defaults to the first top-level class in the file.

impl_name.description: Alternate way to name the class — the plan kind accepts either module_name or impl_name.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-extract-class-cohesive-clusters. Charter: Propose cohesive method/field clusters inside a Java god-class to guide partition decisions before any extract_java_class run.

Protocol (analysis-only — no apply step):

1. Ground the target structurally:
   bbox_code_symbols(project_dir="{{project_dir}}", query="{{module_name}}",
                     languages=["java"], item_kinds=["class_declaration"])
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")
   Confirm the target class exists.

2. Plan the cluster suggestion:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="extract_java_class_cohesive_clusters",
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{source}}",
                      module_name="{{module_name}}",
                      impl_name="{{impl_name}}")
   The response is analysis-only (analysis_only=true, dry_run=true,
   edits=[]) and carries:
     - class {name, package, source_path}
     - suggested_clusters: list of {id, name_hint, item_names,
       move_fields, score, internal_field_touches, internal_calls,
       inbound_calls, outbound_calls, expected_wiring}.
       expected_wiring is one of:
         - "delegate": source class can hold this cluster as a private
           delegate field; no callbacks needed.
         - "callback": this cluster invokes methods still on the source;
           operator must thread those as functional callbacks
           (Runnable/Consumer/Supplier) when extracting.
         - "source_instance": bidirectional coupling — both inbound and
           outbound calls cross the seam. The split is not clean; the
           operator should rethink the partition or share a source
           instance reference.
     - cross_cluster_calls: every method-to-method edge whose endpoints
       fall in different clusters, with from_method/to_method named so
       the operator can audit which seams pay coupling cost.

3. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line summary: class name, number of
     clusters, total cross_cluster_calls, and which clusters have
     expected_wiring="source_instance" (the seams that aren't clean)>).
   When the response surfaces zero or one cluster, say so plainly — the
   class is not god-ish enough to warrant a partition. When two-plus
   clusters appear with zero cross_cluster_calls, that is the cleanest
   possible split and the operator should be told.

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never call any tool outside the refactor persona tool surface.
- Never propose an extract_java_class plan from this atom — that is a
  separate atom (java-extract-cohesive-class) the operator runs after
  reviewing the suggestion.
- Never collapse cross_cluster_calls into a single number; the operator
  needs to see which methods cross the seam.
- Never invent class names from the user prompt — re-derive from
  bbox_code_symbols.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{source}} {{module_name}} {{impl_name}}
